html:
"Slavic tribes" is the map's label, for the year 900, for the Slavic peoples of central Europe, from the Elbe across Bohemia and Poland to the upper Dniester. It is the same world as the Slavonic tribes of the 800 map, a century on.

Around 900 several of these tribes were turning into states:

  • Great Moravia, the strongest of them, broke apart under Magyar attacks soon after 900.
  • In Bohemia the Czechs were gathering under the Přemyslid princes of Prague.
  • On the Vistula and Warta the Polans were ruled by the Piasts, who made Poland and accepted Christianity at the baptism of 966.
  • Between the Elbe and the Oder, Sorbs and other Polabian Slavs held out against the kings of East Francia, who pushed east against them for centuries.

These peoples lived by farming, around fortified towns of wood and earth.
